learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of nine alt texts for one photo is useful or needs work, with at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** alt-text-evaluator
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of nine alt texts for one photo is useful or needs work, with at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Alt Text, Decorative Image (both defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each alt text the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 8 of 9 correct on the first attempt. Reading the four habits is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Longer alt text is always better. (2) "Image of" helps the reader. (3) Empty alt text is safe for any image. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging alt text against stated habits is an Evaluate-level action. Nine alternatives for one photo isolate the differences that matter, so the learner learns what separates a useful description from a poor one. **Content:** The photo, described in words and shown at all times: a school garden's rain barrel under a roof downspout, used in a lesson on reducing runoff. The four habits, shown on request: say what matters in the context; do not begin with "image of"; do not repeat an adjacent caption; never use a filename or a single word. The nine alt texts: | # | Alt text shown to the learner | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | image1.png | Needs work | A filename says nothing about the image. | | 2 | photo | Needs work | One word that says nothing. | | 3 | A rain barrel under a roof downspout collects water from the roof | Useful | It names the object and what it does. | | 4 | Image of a photograph of a barrel | Needs work | It begins with "image of" and does not say what matters. | | 5 | A rain barrel in a school garden collects roof runoff, one way to keep water from flowing onto pavement | Useful | It connects the object to the lesson. | | 6 | A rain barrel at the end of a roof downspout | Useful | It is short and names what is shown and where. | | 7 | A picture of the school garden taken by Ms. Lee on a sunny day with many flowers, a bench, and the principal's car in the background | Needs work | It is long and lists details that do not serve the lesson. | | 8 | (empty alt text) | Needs work | The photo carries information the lesson uses, so it is not decorative. | | 9 | Rain barrel connected to a downspout, holding runoff from the school roof | Useful | It is plain and says what the picture shows and why it matters. | **Provenance:** The photo and the alt texts are written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The habits follow the chapter section "Alt Text". **Rules:** Each alt text has exactly one correct bin. Four are Useful and five Need work. A screen reader reads alt text aloud and announces that the element is an image, so the sim treats "image of" as redundant. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees the photo description, the four habits on request, and one alt text. 2. The learner places the alt text in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After alt text 9 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 9 alt texts in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 9 correct on the first attempt". At 8 or more it adds "You can judge alt text." Below 8 it lists the Why text of each missed alt text. **Starting State:** The photo description and alt text 1 or the first in the shuffled order. The question shown is "Is this alt text useful?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked example of three alt texts for the rain barrel photo agrees with this sim: "photo" needs work and the rain barrel at the end of a roof downspout is useful.
